will_not_do: Click submit on a site whose terms haven't been reviewed and approved, or on any site but Lintel Lab at launch.
Solve, evade or route around a CAPTCHA or any other bot challenge.
Guess eligibility, sponsorship, salary or demographic answers.
Send anything you haven't approved, byte for byte, on the device you approved it for.
Retry a submission it can't confirm. It marks it uncertain and asks you.
Message recruiters or referrers for you. It drafts; you send.
Keep your site logins or cookies in the cloud.
limits: The claim check is strongest on specifics (numbers, tools, employers, titles, degrees). Vague praise that is technically true can pass, and some true sentences are blocked until you rephrase or confirm a fact.
Exactly once is “as far as known”: when the runner dies between the click and the confirmation, Lintel can't know whether the site received it, so it says “submission uncertain” and never retries.
Lab results are from Lintel Lab skins that copy public patterns. Real employer forms vary; adapters are versioned per destination in the registry.
The offline drafter is plain and literal. Drafts read better with a model key, and are checked the same way.
No feature here promises interviews. Interviews per sent application is reported with its interval.
note: Generated by `uv run lintel-evals` against a fresh database, the Lintel Lab and the shipped runner in a headless browser. Nothing is mocked; failing rows stay in the report.
